display.title: Terumah and Tetzaveh: Why Hashem Asked for a Mishkan
display.summary_short: Why the Mishkan was commanded right after the giving of the Torah, and how every Jew becomes a small sanctuary for Hashem through mitzvos.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, aired between Parshas Terumah and Parshas Tetzaveh, which describe building the Mishkan. Uncle Yossi explains one reason it was commanded right after Matan Torah. At Har Sinai the Jewish people saw Hashem's glory so openly that their souls flew out of them, and Hashem revived them with the heavenly dew of revival, the same dew that will bring back the dead at techiyas hameisim. When the revelation ended, they begged to see Hashem's glory again, and Hashem answered: 'Make Me a sanctuary and I will dwell among them.' The Midrash explains 'among them' as within each and every Jew, so even without a Mishkan or Beis HaMikdash today, every Jew is a small sanctuary. Each mitzvah invites the Shechinah to rest on us and makes us a holy nation. He closes with a prayer for the third Beis HaMikdash to descend from heaven with Moshiach.
display.lesson: Every Jew is a small sanctuary, and each mitzvah invites Hashem's presence to rest on us.
